study.title: Ipsilateral Putamen and Insula Activation by Both Left and Right GB34 Acupuncture Stimulation: An fMRI Study on Healthy Participants
study.study_design: Within-subject fMRI study comparing left versus right GB34 acupuncture stimulation in healthy volunteers using a block design with sham and verum acupuncture conditions
study.inclusion_criteria: Right-handed as verified by the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory; no history of any chronic disease, allergy, and neurological or psychiatric disorder
study.exclusion_criteria: History of any chronic disease, allergy, and neurological or psychiatric disorder; not right-handed

conditions.condition_label_exact: sham acupuncture stimulation at left GB34
conditions.timepoint_exact: first scan block (scanning started with the sham acupuncture condition)
conditions.scan_context: fMRI block design; sham acupuncture scan took about 5 minutes
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Needle is inserted approximately 1.0 cm (10 mm) into GB34, which exceeds the 5 mm threshold for full penetration. At this depth the needle reaches muscle/fascia, activating deep mechanoreceptors. Despite being labeled 'sham', the physical depth of tissue engagement classifies it as Level 1.

extraction_notes.note: The paper reports coordinates as 'Talairach coordinates' via Talairach Client, but neuroimaging data were processed using SPM5 with MNI space normalization. There is ambiguity about whether coordinates were natively in MNI space and then converted to Talairach, or originally Talairach. The paper explicitly states 'all local maxima were reported as Talairach coordinates by using Talairach Client,' implying conversion from MNI.
Cluster sizes (in voxels or mm3) are not reported in Table 2 or Table 3; only peak t-values and Talairach coordinates are provided.
Smoothing kernel is not reported for the fMRI preprocessing pipeline.
Expectancy, treatment credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported in this study.
Adverse events are not reported in this study. The paper makes no mention of any adverse events occurring.
No trial registration number is reported.

The paper describes the experimental paradigm as a 'block design' but does not provide the full block structure in explicit detail (e.g., number of blocks, block length, rest periods between conditions) beyond the 5-minute overall duration and the needle rotation protocol.

The deqi questionnaire used is described in reference [31] (Dhond et al. 2008 in Pain), which appears to be a modified version of the Massachusetts General Hospital Acupuncture Sensation Scale (MASS). The instrument name is not explicitly stated in the paper.

The paper reports that all subjects 'reported deqi sensations'; however, the sham condition deqi ratings are not presented separately in Table 1. The Table 1 deqi data appear to reflect acupuncture conditions only, but this is not explicitly confirmed.

The paper states participants' average age was 43.9 (range: 25-66) years in the abstract/methods, but Table 1 reports mean ages of 54.9 ± 2.43 (left group) and 56.58 ± 2.96 (right group). This is an internal inconsistency in the paper.

The reported average age in the methods section (43.9, range 25-66) is inconsistent with the ages reported in Table 1 (54.9 ± 2.43 for left group; 56.58 ± 2.96 for right group). The source of this discrepancy is not explained in the paper.

The paper does not report motion exclusion criteria beyond that participants were instructed not to move and heads were immobilized. No specific motion threshold for exclusion of volumes or participants is described.

The paper refers to scanning starting with the sham acupuncture condition, then structural imaging, then acupuncture. The order appears fixed and not counterbalanced, which is a potential methodological limitation not discussed in the methods.

The correlation analyses (tingling vs. insula/putamen MR signal) in Figure 3 appear to pool data across both left and right GB34 groups combined (n=22), but this is not explicitly stated in the paper.
The paper does not report statistical significance (p-value) for the tingling-insula and tingling-putamen correlations, only R2 values (0.0928 and 0.1048 respectively).
